messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: proposal for syntax/semantics of functions in Stan
parts:
Here’s the current proposal for the function syntax and semantics:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Function-Syntax-and-Semantics-Design

I was going to send it to the user list, but I thought that might just
frustrate people more than make it feel like an open process if I didn’t
take the suggestions. I do not want to add named arguments, nor do I want
to have any Stan variables brought into scope.

And of course, I need to balance ease of implementation with ease of use.

- Bob

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] proposal for syntax/semantics of functions in Stan
parts:
A couple thoughts:

- I'd recommend allowing functions to come after the data blocks and allowing data and transformed data variables to be in scope for the function and subroutine bodies.  I don't see a reason not to do this (but I could be wrong) and it seems like it could be useful.
- I don't see a reason to have a "return void;" option syntactically.  void is not a type we really need (or want) users to be familiar with more than strictly necessary.
- Do variables have to be passed by const reference to subroutines and functions?  If just by reference then this could somewhat avoid the need for multiple returns in the near future.
- Speaking of multiple returns, boost::tuple might be useful here instead of having to define new structures for each function.

Cheers,
Marcus
